# Generated files and the explorer

What the [reference tool](tool.md) writes: the generated files of a project, and the explorer, a view of the map outside the repository.

## Generated files

`check --fix` writes the files of [spec-conformance.md](spec-conformance.md), section 7, and the skill stubs: the component diagram of every unit with children, the index `docs/decisions/index.md` of every unit that has decisions, and the root `AGENTS.md`. The sequence diagram of a scenario and the state diagram of a contract are drawn on demand: `unifold scenario UNIT NAME` and `unifold states UNIT CONTRACT` print them as Markdown, and the explorer shows them. It removes generated files it no longer writes, and it never overwrites a file that lacks the generated marker: a hand-written `AGENTS.md` at the root is reported until its content has moved to `README.md` and `docs/` and the file is deleted. Links to files that do not exist are left out.

A scenario diagram, as `unifold scenario` prints it, shows each lifeline with its name, its kind and what it runs as, once at the top; a table below the steps says what each lifeline does. A picture shows every row of the table beside it. A step wider than 34 characters wraps at a space. A step goes from its caller to its target, as the hop is written: a command, query or callback with a solid arrow and a dashed arrow back with its result; an event with an open arrowhead. The target of a step is active until a lifeline further out makes the next step; a unit below the target acts for it. A step that nothing follows inside leaves no bar and carries its result on its own arrow. When a unit raises an event, the call it was handling has returned, and so has every call that waited for it and does nothing more afterwards; a unit handling an event keeps running; an event from a unit outside the open calls arrives during them. An event that reaches a lifeline with an open bar lands on that bar; only an idle receiver gets a new bar. `parallel` is drawn as a `par` block with `and` between its branches and one `end`, and `repeat` as a `loop`. An included scenario is one step, `scenario <unit>.<name> (<n> steps)`, so that a page shows one level: an arrow from the caller of its first step, with an open arrowhead when that step is an event, or a note on the unit when that caller lies inside the unit; `--expand` opens every include as a shaded block, end to end across levels. The links of the page start at the folder in which the command runs. A note on the provider's lifeline shows each state of a connection whose contract has states, with the name of the contract, after the step that led to it returns. A state diagram, as `unifold states` prints it, shows every row of the table: a part that leaves the state as it is stands inside the state's box, and a part that moves it stands on the arrow to the next state.

## The explorer

`unifold explore` writes the explorer and opens it in the browser: one HTML page with the unit tree, the component, context and architecture diagram of every unit with its tables, every document of every unit, and a page per scenario that shows its path on the map. Without `-o` the page goes to the temporary folder of the system, outside the repository; `-o FILE` or `-o DIR` writes it where a project publishes it, `--no-open` leaves the browser closed, and `--mermaid FILE` embeds Mermaid so that the page works offline.
